knowledge_point.title: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}6 & 6 & 9 \\ 10 & 2 & 10 \\ 5 & -6 & -4\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}-24 & 0 & -21 \\ 10 & 2 & 10 \\ 35 & 0 & 26\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below $a_{22}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}6 & 6 & 9 \\ 10 & 2 & 10 \\ 5 & -6 & -4\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}-3R_{2}}\begin{bmatrix}-24 & 0 & -21 \\ 10 & 2 & 10 \\ 5 & -6 & -4\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{3}:=R_{3}+3R_{2}}\begin{bmatrix}-24 & 0 & -21 \\ 10 & 2 & 10 \\ 35 & 0 & 26\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}-3R_{2}$ and $R_{3}:=R_{3}+3R_{2}$.
